obtained.how: the human's own copies of both MDIFW survey sheets (docs/research_notes/fetched/hot_brook_lake_upper.pdf and hot_brook_lake_lower.pdf; maine.gov refuses scripted fetches), indexed with getsrc --file as MDIFW_1949 (Upper) and MDIFW_1949.lower (Lower). Each sheet is two scanned pages (a typed text page and a hand-lettered sounding map) with an OCR text layer; every value below was read on the rendered page images (MDIFW_1949.p1/p2.png, MDIFW_1949.lower.p1/p2.png), the soundings at 2-3x zoom

bibliography.checked_against: both sheets (title lines, survey and revision lines, funding line)
bibliography.note: The text pages are headed 'HOT BROOK LAKE, UPPER' and 'HOT BROOK LAKE, LOWER'; the maps 'UPPER HOT BROOK LAKE' (912 ACRES) and 'LOWER HOT BROOK LAKE' (713 ACRES). Both read 'Surveyed - August, 1949 (Revised - 1965,2004)', 'Maine Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife', 'Funded in part by the Federal Aid in Restoration Act under Federal Project F-28-P'. BOTH sheets carry the code 'L1072F' (Lower's MIDAS number is 1072), so the Upper sheet cannot be used to confirm Upper's MIDAS 1076. The Lower file is at .../washington/hot_brook_lake_lower.pdf (the entry gives both URLs correctly).

claims.claim: Upper's deepest water, 5.5 m (18 ft), is in a north basin beside the outlet; a narrows of 13-16 ft leads south to a broad basin of 11-14 ft, edged along the south shore by a shelf 2-10 ft deep
claims.location: Upper map, p. 2
claims.conditions: the outlet leaves the north tip; the 18-ft soundings are the third row of the north basin, about 0.7 km (225 px at 3.16 m/px) south of where the outlet leaves (the row nearest the outlet reads 3 4 5 4); the narrows rows read 8 10 16 16 15 13 and 13 16 14 5 (5 at the east shore); the four broad south-basin rows read mostly 11-14 ft (one 9, shore values 3-8); the southernmost row reads 4 5 9 4 3 2 8 8 2 10 10 9 9 8 4
claims.note: 'beside the outlet' is loose (the deep row is in the outlet's basin, ~0.7 km from the outlet itself); 'in the north basin, the outlet's basin' is exact.

claims.claim: in Lower most soundings read 9-12 ft (2.7-3.7 m), the deepest, 13 ft (4.0 m), lies south of center, and the large eastern bay is 4-11 ft (1.2-3.4 m) deep
claims.location: Lower map, p. 2
claims.conditions: 34 of the 63 soundings are 9-12 ft (54 %); the single 13 lies in the sixth of ten rows from the north end (the inlet is at the south tip, the outlet on the NE shore); the only soundings in the eastern bay are the row running into it, 11 11 9 4
claims.note: 'most' is a bare majority (54 %). The 'long central trough inside the 10-ft contour' is MDIFW 2024's (the 1949 map has no contours). MDIFW 2024 carries no soundings, so cite MDIFW 1949 alone for the sounding ranges (as the MDIFW_2024 evidence also says).

claims.claim: both sheets carry a second line, '75 feet – 71 °F' (21.7 °C), a depth impossible in lakes of 18 and 13 ft; if near-bottom, the column was within 1.7 °C top to bottom
claims.location: Upper and Lower sheets, p. 1 (text page, 'Temperatures', second line)
claims.quote: 75 feet - 71°F.
claims.conditions: typed, not an OCR artefact: the page images show '75 feet - 71°F.' on both sheets, beside 'Maximum depth - 18 feet' (Upper) and '13 feet' (Lower)
claims.note: (71 − 32)/1.8 = 21.7 °C; 74 − 71 = 3 °F = 1.67 °C. The 'garbled near-bottom reading or template error' is the paper's interpretation, correctly labelled as such. (hot_brook_lake_records.md's 'OCR error' hypothesis is ruled out by the images.)

notes: Both sheets read in full on the page images (the OCR layer is close but writes 'horn pout' and '71OF'). Nearly everything the paper takes from them checks, including the project tallies (83 + 63 = 146 soundings; means 3.25 and 2.71 m). Changes for the rewrite: (1) §2.5 and Table 3 quote 'horn pout'; the sheets print 'hornpout'. (2) Table 1's row label and §2.2's 'MDIFW's 1949 planimetry' give a method and a date the sheets do not state (area as printed; method and date not stated). (3) 'as revised in 2004' (§2.5, §2.10) and the temperatures' 'August 1949' date are inferences from 'Surveyed - August, 1949 (Revised - 1965,2004)': likely, but the sheets do not say which text belongs to which revision. (4) The sheets' bag limit is not called 'daily' (§3.3.x line 728). (5) src/config.js:932 calls the 71 °F reading 'at the bottom'; the sheet says '75 feet'. (6) §2.3's 'Hot Brook is the main inflow' is not on the sheets, which name no inlet for Upper. (7) §3.5.6's 22-25 °C floor sits just above the sheets' 21.7 °C. Also: both sheets carry the code 'L1072F', so they cannot confirm Upper's MIDAS 1076; the Upper map title is cut off at the left ('...O. AND BANCROFT TWP.'); one mark on the Upper map ('0b', row 7, a different hand) is not a depth. The research note maine_dep_lakes_data_2025.md attributes '"slightly turbid", brown water' to 1949; neither sheet says it. show.mjs lists §3.3, §3.4.1, §3.5.1, §3.5.6, §3.5.7, §3.5.8 without printing their paragraphs: they are covered above (02_synthesis lines 601, 728, 738; 03_synthesis lines 34, 314, 360, 394, 498, 1323) plus §4.1 (04_model line 22) and §6.3 (05_discussion line 59).
